assertions.description: ServiceWorkerContainer.prototype.register is a function — the precondition for a worker whose install handler calls InstallEvent.addRoutes() (InstallEvent is only exposed in worker scope, so addRoutes itself is checked by the race-rule-installs row).
PerformanceResourceTiming exposes workerMatchedSourceType, the field that reports a request matched a race-network-and-fetch-handler rule.
A real worker scoped to this feature installs a static routing rule with source 'race-network-and-fetch-handler' (addRoutes resolves).
assertions.test: Requires registering the feature's service worker (async, scope-bound). Observed live on /v159/serviceworker-static-routing-distinct-typeerror-message-for-cancelled-race-netwo/cancellation-lab/ (section 1 reports the addRoutes outcome).

assertions.description: When the fetch handler's respondWith() settles before the deduplicated race request receives headers, fetch(event.request) rejects with TypeError("The service worker race-network-and-fetch-handler request was cancelled before 'fetch()' settled.").
assertions.test: Requires the feature's service worker, a header-delayed server route and a race; Chrome 159 or a build with --enable-features=ServiceWorkerRaceNetworkRequestAbortedErrorMessage. Run /v159/serviceworker-static-routing-distinct-typeerror-message-for-cancelled-race-netwo/cancellation-lab/ with the timer below the delay.

assertions.description: The cancellation rejection is still a TypeError, so existing instanceof TypeError handling keeps working.
assertions.test: Observed by the worker report's isTypeError field in the cancellation lab and scenario matrix.

assertions.description: A genuine network failure on a raced request (redirect loop, not ERR_ABORTED) still rejects with TypeError("Failed to fetch").
assertions.test: Observed in the scenario matrix's redirect-loop row on /v159/serviceworker-static-routing-distinct-typeerror-message-for-cancelled-race-netwo/scenario-matrix/.
